chunks: He who describes Him limits Him. He who limits Him numbers Him. He who numbers Him rejects His eternity. He who said 'how' sought a description for Him. He who said 'where' bounded Him. He is the Knower even though there be nothing to be known. He is the Sustainer even though there be nothing to be sustained. He is the Powerful even though there be nothing to be overpowered.

key_terms.حَيَّزَهُ: bounded Him / assigned Him a place

ai.seo_question: How does Nahj al-Balagha describe the limits of human understanding of God's essence?
ai.summary: This passage, often cited in Shia kalām (theology) to refute anthropomorphism (tashbih), establishes that any linguistic description implies limitation, thereby necessitating divine transcendence. It underscores the principle that God’s attributes are identical to His essence, existing independently of created counterparts, a view central to the Akhbari and Usuli debates on divine names. The text serves as a foundational argument for understanding God as the absolute subject without an object, reinforcing the concept of tawhid al-sifat.
